# Auto-Planning UK

> Auto-Planning UK generates the drawing set a UK householder planning
> application needs: a Location Plan at 1:1250 or 1:2500 on Ordnance Survey
> mapping with a red-line site boundary, a Block Plan with boundary
> clearances, Existing and Proposed Roof Plans, all four
> Existing and Proposed Elevations at 1:100 with scale bars, a Schedule of
> Materials and a generated Planning Statement — bundled as one Planning
> Portal-ready PDF.

## What it is for

Householder applications of these types, chosen per case and used to word the
generated Planning Statement and schedule:

- Extensions — single or two-storey, porches, conservatories.
- Loft conversions and dormers.
- Outbuildings and detached garages.
- Roof covering replacement (re-roofs) that need permission because the
  property is in a conservation area, under an Article 4 direction, or
  otherwise has restricted permitted development rights.
- Other external alterations — windows, cladding, render, rooflights.
- Users: householders, and the builders, roofers and small design practices
  preparing applications for their customers.

## How it works

1. Search the postcode; draw the red-line boundary around the whole plot on
   OS mapping; capture the location plan at a true print scale.
2. Model the building as parametric blocks (gable/hip/mono-pitch/flat roofs,
   pitch, eaves, windows, doors, rooflights, chimneys) — building heights can
   be prefilled from OS building-height data. The proposed model starts as a
   copy of the existing one and diverges only where the works do.
3. Download one PDF with a page per drawing, each with an accurate scale
   bar, north arrow where required, drawing numbers and a materials schedule.

## Key facts

- Every drawing's scale is correct by construction (geometry is laid out in
  physical page millimetres).
- Mapping: Ordnance Survey Data Hub (vector tiles, NGD building heights).
- The tool does not provide legal or planning advice; users should check
  their local planning authority's validation checklist.
